title.justification: The title is directly extracted from the paper and encapsulates the focus of the research on using connectomics to classify mammals.

extractions.description: The paper explores the use of connectomic data to classify mammalian species. By standardizing neural circuit reconstruction techniques, it compares connectome data across 124 species of mammals. The research aims to assess inter-species variations in neural connectivity and how these connectome organizations correlate with traditional taxonomies based on morphology and genetics. Overall, the study attempts to provide insights into the evolution of neural circuits and their relationship to behavior.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: While the paper provides valuable insights into the connectomics of mammals, the theme of Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development is not a focus. The paper centers on the biological and evolutionary aspects of mammalian neural circuits rather than any specific environmental or sustainability goals.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: Mammalian taxonomies are conventionally defined by morphological traits and genetics. How species differ in terms of neural circuits and whether inter-species differences in neural circuit organization conform to these taxonomies is unknown.

primary_category.justification: The primary focus of the paper is on biological science rather than any directly tied Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development issue. It deciphers mammalian taxonomy via connectomic similarities, which does not align with any categories of sustainable development listed.
primary_category.quote: Here we comprehensively chart connectome organization across the mammalian phylogenetic spectrum using a common reconstruction protocol.

secondary_categories.justification: There are no secondary Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development themes in this paper as its primary focus remains strictly on the taxonomy of mammals via their neural networks.
secondary_categories.quote: While comparative analysis can focus on commonalities among mammalian connectomes and identify universal wiring principles, it can also be used to systematically explore differences among connectomes that confer specific adaptive advantages.

primary_sub_category.justification: There is no specific sub-category that the paper aligns with as it does not address any direct climate or ecological sustainability themes.
primary_sub_category.quote: By encoding connectomes into a common frame of reference, these findings establish a foundation for investigating how neural circuits change over phylogeny, forging a link from genes to circuits to behaviour.

new_primary_category.quote: We analyze the mammalian MRI (MaMI) data set, a database that encompasses high-resolution ex vivo structural and diffusion magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scans of 124 species across 12 taxonomic orders and 5 superorders, collected using a single protocol on a single scanner.
